ques: Look up the pronunciation, definition, and example sentence for the word "ubiquitous" in UK and US English.
answer:
**ubiquitous** (adjective) — Cambridge Dictionary, https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/ubiquitous

**UK (British entry; labelled "formal or humorous")**
- Pronunciation: UK /juːˈbɪk.wɪ.təs/. The same entry also lists US /juːˈbɪk.wə.t̬əs/.
- Definition: seeming to be everywhere.
- Example: "Leather is very much in fashion this season, as is the ubiquitous denim."

**US (American Dictionary entry)**
- Pronunciation: US /jʊˈbɪk·wɪ·t̬əs, ju-/
- Definition: found or existing everywhere.
- Example: "The eel grass limpet used to be ubiquitous on the New England coast."

ques: Check out Text Embeddings Inference in Hugging face's Doc to summarise the strengths of the toolkit.
answer:
Per the Text Embeddings Inference (TEI) docs, TEI is a toolkit for efficient deployment and serving of open-source text embedding models. Its main strengths are:

- **Simple deployment:** It needs no model graph compilation step.
- **Light on resources:** It has small Docker images and fast boot times, which makes true serverless use possible.
- **Dynamic batching:** Batching is token-based, which makes better use of resources during inference.
- **Optimized inference:** It uses Flash Attention, Candle and cuBLASLt, with optimized transformer code.
- **Fast weight loading:** It loads Safetensors weights, which also speeds up boot.
- **Production-ready:** It supports distributed tracing through OpenTelemetry and exports Prometheus metrics.
- **Model support:** It delivers high-performance extraction for popular models such as FlagEmbedding, Ember, GTE and E5.
- **Benchmarks:** The page includes latency and throughput charts for BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 on an NVIDIA A10 at 512 tokens, for batch sizes 1 and 32. I didn't read the chart results, so I can't say what they show.

Source: https://huggingface.co/docs/text-embeddings-inference/index

ques: Let g(x) be the integral of x^2 cos(2x). Write the expression of g(x).
answer:
**g(x) = ∫ x² cos(2x) dx = ¼[(2x² − 1) sin(2x) + 2x cos(2x)] + C**

This is the same as (x²/2 − ¼) sin(2x) + ½ x cos(2x) + C.

I got this from Wolfram|Alpha's "Indefinite integral" result for "integrate x^2 cos(2x)": https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=integrate+x%5E2+cos%282x%29. The page renders its results as images, so I read the expression from the images' alt text rather than from a screenshot.

ques: Determine the convergence or divergence of the series Σ (n=1 to ∞) of 1/(n^3 + 1).
answer:
The series Σ (n=1 to ∞) 1/(n³+1) **converges**. Wolfram|Alpha gives this result, and its sum is about 0.68650.

This also follows from direct comparison. For n ≥ 1, 1/(n³+1) < 1/n³, and Σ 1/n³ is a convergent p-series because p = 3 > 1.

Source: https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=convergence+of+sum+1%2F%28n%5E3%2B1%29+from+n%3D1+to+infinity
